chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from those whom he mentioned from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
About a man who takes something for a man, then it becomes clear to him (or he changes his mind), so he gives it to someone else, he said: There is no harm.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible
key_terms.يَبْدُو: It becomes clear / he changes his mind

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to give a reserved gift or item to someone else instead of the original person?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that reserving a Zakat item for a specific recipient does not create a binding ownership transfer (qabd) until actual possession occurs, allowing the giver discretion to redirect it. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic distinction between mere intention and legal possession in charitable distributions, ensuring flexibility in fulfilling the spiritual intent of Zakat. It reflects the practical application of property rights in early Islamic society where formal contracts were less rigid than in later fiqh developments.

en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthman from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, or abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhim al-Salam,
about a man who keeps something for someone then for some reason gives it to someone else, has said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
